name: Neck-Shoulder Tension (Mild)
description: 4-phase program for mild tension: Relaxation, Mobilization, Strengthening, Functional Training
pain_rule: Perform exercises at pain <= 3/10. Reduce load if tension increases.
evidence_base: Gross et al. (2015): Exercise for mechanical neck disorders
Jull et al. (2008): Cranio-cervical flexion training
Falla et al. (2012): Specific deep cervical flexor exercise
Ylinen et al. (2003): Active neck muscle training in chronic neck pain
progression_criteria: Phase 1 -> 2: 10 days, min. 3 sessions, tension significantly reduced
Phase 2 -> 3: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, good mobility, pain <= 3/10
Phase 3 -> 4: 14 days, min. 4 sessions, strength built up, pain <= 3/10

phase_education.1:
**Phase 1: Relaxation & Pain Relief**

In this phase, the focus is on relaxing tense muscles and gentle mobilization. Tension often arises from stress, poor posture, or one-sided strain.

**Goal:** Release tension and regain initial mobility.

**Strategy:**
- Targeted breathing exercises to relax the shoulder-neck region
- Gentle activation of the deep cervical muscles
- Stretching exercises for shortened muscles
- Short, frequent exercise sessions

**Scientific Basis:** Breathing exercises and gentle mobilization reduce muscle tension more effectively than rest (Gross et al., 2015). Activating the deep cervical flexors improves postural control.
phase_education.2:
**Phase 2: Mobilization & Control**

You have resolved the acute tension! Now we improve mobility and train motor control of the neck-shoulder region.

**Goal:** Improved mobility and neuromuscular control.

**Strategy:**
- Increase endurance of the deep cervical flexors
- Scapular stabilization for better shoulder blade control
- Thoracic mobility for upright posture
- Quality over quantity

**Scientific Basis:** The CCF training method by Jull et al. (2008) is the gold standard for rehabilitation of the deep cervical flexors. Thoracic mobility reduces compensatory neck strain.
phase_education.3:
**Phase 3: Strengthening**

Your mobility has improved. Now we strengthen the neck-shoulder muscles to prevent tension long-term.

**Goal:** Build strength and load capacity.

**Strategy:**
- Progressive strengthening with controlled movements
- Isometric exercises for neck strength
- Scapular strengthening for shoulder stability
- Slow tempo for maximum effect

**Scientific Basis:** Progressive strengthening of the cervico-scapulothoracic muscles significantly reduces tension and pain (Ylinen et al., 2003). The combination of isometric and dynamic training shows the best long-term results.
phase_education.4:
**Phase 4: Functional Integration**

You are almost there! In this phase, we integrate your strength into everyday movements and build a maintenance program.

**Goal:** Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention.

**Strategy:**
- Functional exercises for daily life and work
- Workplace micro-breaks as routine
- Self-massage techniques
- Maintenance training 3x/week

**Scientific Basis:** Integration into everyday movements and regular micro-breaks at the workplace are crucial for the long-term prevention of neck-shoulder tension.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing with Shoulder Relaxation
exercises.description: Seated or lying on your back. Place hands on your abdomen. Breathe deeply through the nose into the belly (4 sec), exhale slowly through the mouth (6 sec). With each exhale, consciously let the shoulders drop and relax the neck muscles.

exercises.name: Chin Tuck
exercises.description: Sit upright, gaze straight ahead. Gently retract the chin, as if making a double chin. Lengthen the neck, push the back of the head upward. Hold the position, then slowly release.

exercises.name: Gentle Cervical Mobility (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Slowly tilt the head forward, return to neutral. Then tilt backward (look at the ceiling), return. Tilt to the left, return. Tilt to the right, return. Each direction slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.description: Sit upright. Right hand grips under the chair. Tilt head to the left, gently place left hand on the head (no pressure!). Feel a comfortable stretch on the side of the neck. Hold 30 seconds, switch sides.

exercises.name: Scapular Setting
exercises.description: Sit upright, arms hanging loosely. Gently draw the shoulder blades back and down together, without raising the shoulders. Hold the position, then slowly release.

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.description: Sit upright. Slightly rotate the head to the left, then tilt forward and down (look toward your left armpit). Right hand grips under the chair. Feel the stretch at the right neck-shoulder junction. Hold 30 seconds, switch sides.

exercises.name: CCF Endurance Progression
exercises.description: Lying on your back, head on a pillow. Slowly and deliberately tuck the chin (activate deep cervical flexors). Gradually increase hold time to 10-15 seconds. Quality over duration - take a break when control fades.

exercises.name: Prone Y/T/W Lifts
exercises.description: Lying face down on the floor. Alternately lift arms in Y-position (diagonally upward), T-position (sideways), and W-position (elbows bent) off the floor. Squeeze shoulder blades together, hold 2 seconds, lower.

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.description: Stand with your back against the wall. Place arms in 90-degree position against the wall (forearms on the wall). Slowly slide arms upward, maintaining wall contact. Actively draw shoulder blades down.

exercises.name: Thoracic Rotation (Open Book)
exercises.description: Side-lying, knees bent. Slowly open the top arm to the other side, rotating the thoracic spine. Eyes follow the hand. Hold 3 seconds at end range, return. Keep hip position stable.

exercises.name: Band Rows with Scapular Guidance
exercises.description: Attach resistance band to a door handle in front of you. Grip the band, pull elbows back. Consciously perform scapular retraction. Slowly return. Keep shoulders down.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
exercises.description: Side-lying, top arm at the body, elbow bent 90 degrees. Slowly rotate the forearm upward (external rotation). Elbow stays at the body. Slowly return. Optionally add light weight (0.5-1 kg).
exercises.intensity: Light - control more important than weight

exercises.name: Neck Flexor Endurance (Supine)
exercises.description: Lying on your back. Tuck the chin and lift the head slightly off the surface. Hold position. If trembling or loss of control occurs, immediately lower and rest.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shoulder Shrugs (3-0-3 Tempo)
exercises.description: Standing, hold dumbbells at your sides. Raise shoulders upward for 3 seconds, briefly hold at the top, lower for 3 seconds in a controlled manner. Specifically strengthen the upper trapezius.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Band Face Pulls
exercises.description: Attach resistance band at face height. Grip band with both hands, pull toward the ears. Keep elbows high, squeeze shoulder blades together. Slowly return. Strengthens posterior shoulder and middle trapezius.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Prone I/Y/T with Light Weight
exercises.description: Lying face down. With light weights (0.5-1 kg), lift arms in I-position (straight forward), Y-position, and T-position off the floor. Actively squeeze shoulder blades together. Hold 2 seconds.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Isometric Neck Work (4 Directions)
exercises.description: Sit upright. Press hand against the head: front, back, left, right. Head holds position against hand resistance (no movement). 10 seconds per direction. Build force slowly and release slowly.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Push-Up Plus (Serratus Activation)
exercises.description: Push-up position (or against the wall for beginners). Perform a regular push-up, at the top push shoulder blades extra forward (protraction). Activates the serratus anterior for scapular stability.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Overhead Press
exercises.description: Standing or seated. Dumbbells at shoulder height. Press up in a controlled manner until arms are nearly extended. Slowly return to shoulder height. Keep core stable, no arching the back.
exercises.phase_goal: Build strength and load capacity of the neck-shoulder region

exercises.name: Rows with Thoracic Rotation
exercises.description: Single-arm band row: grip band, pull elbow back, then rotate thoracic spine toward the pulling side. Combines scapular retraction with thoracic mobility. Slow and controlled.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Workplace Micro-Break (3-in-1)
exercises.description: At the desk: 1) Chin tuck (hold 5 sec), 2) Squeeze shoulder blades together (hold 5 sec), 3) Extend thoracic spine and open arms (hold 5 sec). Repeat every 60-90 minutes. Ideal as a screen break.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Cervicoscapular Circuit
exercises.description: Circuit training: 1) Chin tuck 10x, 2) Shoulder shrugs 10x, 3) Band face pull 10x, 4) Wall slides 10x, 5) Thoracic rotation 8x per side. 30 sec rest between exercises. 2 complete rounds.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Self-Massage Upper Trapezius & Suboccipital
exercises.description: With fingers or tennis ball: 1) Massage the upper trapezius along the shoulder-neck line (2 min), 2) Work the suboccipital muscles at the base of the skull with circular fingertip movements (2 min), 3) Gentle pressure on painful points until tension eases (1 min).
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention

exercises.name: Maintenance Training (3x/Week)
exercises.description: Compact program for long-term prevention: 1) Chin tuck 3x10, 2) Band face pull 3x12, 3) Shoulder shrugs 3x12, 4) Wall slides 2x12, 5) Upper trapezius stretch 2x30s. Total duration approx. 15-20 minutes.
exercises.phase_goal: Long-term freedom from symptoms and prevention
